text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] GPU pool prod-us-west saturated (90%+). Autoscaler unable to provision new nodes: scale_limit_reached. Queue length for /v1/generate on redwood/gptx-ctx32k-v3 increased from 12 -> 420 in 8m. Error rate (429/503) spiked to 18%. paging: true.

oncall-ml: ack. paging oncall. I'm looking. First suspicion: the v3 rollout changed default context handling (kv-cache retention + longer implicit context) — see recent deploy 1798999800.

mike: I'm on call as well. Observed GPU mem pressure on pods with replica_id 7-10, OOMs on kvcache shards. Autoscaler logs show low CPU usage but GPU allocation failed due to overcommit guard.

sara: Customer impact: CS reported increased API errors for customer AcmeAnalytics on embeddings+content-summarize. CS ticket #4321 opened. @cs-rep, can you DM them status?

cs-rep: pinged customer, they report timeouts and a few failed production jobs. No SLA breach yet but latency > 10s for some requests. They've asked for ETA.

kevin: quick diag: payload sizes stable, but average requested max_tokens jumped (clients are sending longer prompt windows). The new model variant keeps kv-cache longer by default which is increasing per-request GPU memory footprint.

jess: logs: here are the autoscaler error lines:
```
2026-03-14T15:07:12Z autoscaler: request_scale up for pool=prod-us-west count=8 failed: scale_limit_reached=8 configured_max_nodes=128 current_nodes=128
2026-03-14T15:08:03Z scheduler: pod create failed: insufficient GPU memory on node gpu-node-74
2026-03-14T15:09:41Z runtime: kv-cache alloc failure: need=2.4G available=1.1G
```

oncall-ml: thanks. Two parallel mitigation tracks: 1) immediate traffic routing to reduce GPU pressure 2) longer-term fix (rollback or model config tweak). I'll coordinate.

mike: mitigation step 1: pause rollout to redwood/gptx-ctx32k-v3 across prod clusters. Executing API call:
```bash
# block new variant traffic -> route 100% back to redwood/gptx-ctx32k-v2
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/rollouts/pause -d '{"model":"redwood/gptx-ctx32k-v3","env":"prod"}'
```
mike: paused. Confirmed routing change propagated to 3 regions (us-west, eu-west, ap-south).

ops-lead: good. Any quick wins to clear queue?

oncall-ml: we can temporarily reduce max_context_length for the v3 variant (but it's paused) and trigger a cache eviction across running pods to reclaim memory. Or set kv-cache TTL shorter. Also we can enable fallback routing to CPU-backed small model for non-critical low-priority requests.

kevin: initiating cache purge on nodes in prod-us-west: `kubectl exec -n runtime -- pod/gpu-node-7 -- sh -c "curl -sS localhost:8080/admin/kv/purge"` — running now.

jess: purge completed on 7/10 nodes. Memory freed ~18GB total. Queue decreased from 420 -> 260 in 9m. 429s still observed.

mike: enabling soft-fallback policy for embeddings endpoints (route 25% to cpu-emb-compact model) to relieve GPU-bound throughput. Applying config:
```json
{"route":"/v1/embeddings","policy":"soft_fallback","fallback_model":"redwood/emb-compact-v1","split":0.25}
```

oncall-ml: note: soft-fallback increases latency for those requests but reduces GPU pressure. Rolling now.

cs-rep: updated AcmeAnalytics: we reduced overall load and paused new variant. They appreciate the proactive update.

ops-lead: still seeing autoscaler limit messages — why can't we spin up more nodes? Configured_max_nodes is 128 and we're at 128, is there a runaway allocation from other pools?

jess: cross-check: prod-gpu-reserved appears to be consumed by training jobs launched by infra-team's scheduled batch. I see a scheduled run at 15:00 that started and consumed 40 nodes.

kevin: I'm disabling the scheduled training batch now (infra notified). Will free ~40 GPUs in ~5min.

mike: manual emergency scale up requested with infra: asking cloud provider for a soft quota increase while we stabilize. @ops-lead please escalate.

ops-lead: on it—opening support case with cloud provider + internal quota runbook. ETA ~30-45m for additional capacity.

oncall-ml: intermediate action: apply per-pod memory caps to avoid single pods monopolizing memory and causing OOM churn. Also lower default batch size for v2 to reduce per-request GPU memory. Applying config: `runtime.pool.prod-us-west.pod_memory_limit=80G` and `model.redwood/gptx-ctx32k-v2.batch_size=8`

jess: changes pushed. After memory caps, observed fewer OOMs and less pod churn. Queue dropped to ~90. Error rate down to 6%. Latency median improved but p95 still elevated.

mike: we should do a controlled rollback of any remaining v3 traffic in other regions where rollout may have continued (double-check eu-west).

kevin: eu-west had only 2% v3 traffic, I forced route back to v2. ap-south had none. All regions now on v2.

oncall-ml: summary of mitigations completed:
- paused v3 rollout
- purged kvcache on affected nodes
- applied pod memory caps and reduced batch sizes
- enabled soft-fallback to cpu embeddings for low-priority traffic
- disabled scheduled training batch that consumed reserved GPUs
- opened cloud provider quota request (in flight)

sara: CS update: informed AcmeAnalytics about rollback and mitigations; they're testing and will report if they still see errors.

cs-rep: Acme responded: 'thanks—looks much better, a few older jobs still retrying but error rate reduced.'

ops-lead: handoff: I'm taking second-shift for monitoring until quota increase lands. @mike, @oncall-ml please add any outstanding action items to the incident doc.

mike: action items I have:
- postmortem: root cause appears to be model config change that extended kv-cache retention + clients sending longer implicit contexts. Need a guardrail: block rollouts that increase memory footprint > 10% without perf target.
- add automated preflight simulation that runs a mem/kv footprint estimate before promoting model to prod.
- ensure scheduled training jobs are isolated from prod GPU pools (enforce pool-level reservations).

oncall-ml: I will create a hotfix to make kv-cache retention configurable per-deployment with safe defaults, and add a canary test that runs a high-concurrency synthetic workload to exercise mem pressure.

jess: monitoring follow-up: add alert when queue > 100 for >5m and GPU_pool_util >85% and autoscaler_denied=true.

ops-lead: timeline note: initial alert 1799001234 -> paused rollout 1799001348 -> purge + caps 1799001600 -> queue under control 1799003100 -> cloud quota request opened 1799003600 -> handoff 1799004200.

mike: I'm documenting affected customers and any billing/credits decisions we should consider. Will coordinate with finance if needed.

oncall-ml: marking incident as mitigated for now but not resolved. Leaving thread open for postmortem and follow-up.

incident-bot: incident severity set to Sev2. Incident channel updated. Runbook link: https://internal/redwood/runbooks/model-rollout-memory-regression

ops-lead: Handoff to me. Monitoring for 3h, will escalate if error rate creeps back. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
